solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Dog training ahead of test? It requires careful manipulation (8)

indicatorNotes.ahead of: puts PUP and PE in front of TRY

blocks.note: a pup is a young dog

annotation.surface: An owner drills a puppy before some trial, a task that calls for a delicate touch.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface keeps you thinking of dog handling, but the manipulation is of strings: a puppeteer's hands work the figure.
annotation.definitionFit: Puppetry is the art of working puppets, which depends on careful manipulation of strings or hands.

entries.clue: Official caught in tricky situation on the runway? (9)

annotation.surface: A match official gets into a scrape out on an airstrip.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: things done on the runway before take-off are preflight, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: Preflight checks and procedures happen on the runway, before the plane takes off.

entries.clue: Flatten out gold beneath thin sheet of silver? (7)

indicatorNotes.beneath: in a down clue, AU is written below PLATE

blocks.note: plate is a thin coating of silver (or other metal), as in silver plate
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

annotation.surface: A metalworker hammers gold under a thin layer of silver.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flatten out' sits comfortably in the metalworking picture, but it is the definition: to plateau is to level off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: prices or growth that plateau stop rising and stay level, as a graph line goes flat.

entries.clue: Make charming final piece on organ (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, END sits on top of EAR

blocks.note: the end is the final piece
the ear is an organ of hearing

annotation.surface: An organist plays a charming last number.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks like the church instrument, but it is the body part.
annotation.definitionFit: To endear someone is to make them liked, to make them charming to others.

entries.clue: Providing corrective action in respect of me fizzling out (9)

blocks.note: something fizzling out is dying away

annotation.surface: Someone takes steps to rescue their own flagging energy.
annotation.walkthrough: RE is the memo-heading word for 'regarding'.
annotation.definitionFit: Remedying something is putting it right, taking corrective action.

entries.clue: Summit where clubs vote to accept overseas capital (6)

indicatorNotes.to accept: C and X take LIMA inside them

blocks.note: Lima is the capital of Peru
a vote is marked with a cross, X

annotation.surface: At a summit meeting, club delegates vote to admit a foreign capital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Summit' suggests a political conference, but it is simply a peak.
annotation.definitionFit: A climax is the highest point of something, its summit.

entries.clue: Lesser celeb’s monastic life devoid of love (1-6)

indicatorNotes.devoid of: something devoid of a thing lacks it entirely, so CLOISTER must go without its O

blocks.note: the cloister stands for secluded monastic life
love = nil in tennis, the letter O; removed

annotation.surface: A minor celebrity takes up a celibate monk's life.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is 'is', linking definition to wordplay rather than a possessive.
annotation.definitionFit: A C-lister is a celebrity of the third rank, below the A- and B-list.

entries.clue: Fellow almost entirely overwhelmed by daft vernacular (9)

indicatorNotes.entirely overwhelmed by: MAT is wholly surrounded by IDIOTIC

blocks.note: fellow = MATE, short of its last letter

annotation.surface: A man is swamped by a silly way of talking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Almost entirely' reads as one phrase, but it splits: 'almost' trims MATE, 'entirely overwhelmed by' puts it inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Vernacular speech is idiomatic: natural, everyday native language.

entries.clue: A plane maybe circling popular race venue (7)

indicatorNotes.circling: to circle something is to go right round it, so TREE wraps around IN

blocks.note: a plane is a kind of tree

annotation.surface: An aircraft circles a well-loved racecourse.
annotation.walkthrough: The plane is the tree, not an aircraft. AINTREE is the racecourse near Liverpool where the Grand National horse race is run.
annotation.definitionFit: Aintree is a famous horse-racing course, home of the Grand National.

entries.clue: Significant time to worry about losing face (3)

indicatorNotes.losing face: CARE drops its first letter, its face

annotation.surface: A moment of worry about being humiliated.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Losing face' looks like humiliation, but here the face of a word is its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An era is a period marked out by some notable event or character, which is what makes the time significant.

entries.clue: Protest ignited India towards destruction (10)

blocks.note: a demo is a protest march
India is I in the NATO alphabet
on = towards, as in marching on the capital

annotation.surface: A demonstration sparks unrest across India that heads for ruin.
annotation.walkthrough: Each word of the protest story turns into its own short piece, strung together in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually of buildings knocked down, though a sports team can also suffer a demolition.

entries.clue: Heading for shelter from conflict in city (8)

indicatorNotes.in: conflict placed in the city means WAR sits inside the word LEEDS

blocks.note: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England

annotation.surface: Refugees flee fighting in a city in search of safety.
annotation.walkthrough: The picture is of refugees, but the definition is nautical: to head leewards is to move towards the sheltered side, away from the wind.
annotation.definitionFit: Leewards means towards the lee, the side sheltered from the wind.

entries.clue: It contains stuff from the east, infused with a soy-based sauce (6)

indicatorNotes.contains: IT holds the rest inside it
indicatorNotes.from the east: in an across clue, read from right to left, so RAM becomes MAR
indicatorNotes.infused with: A is added to the reversed stuff

blocks.note: used as it stands, split to hold the rest
to stuff is to RAM, turned round

annotation.surface: A label describes a sauce made with eastern ingredients and soy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun (ingredients) but is the verb: to ram is to stuff.
annotation.definitionFit: Tamari is a Japanese sauce brewed from soybeans, usually with little or no wheat, a specific example of the category.

entries.clue: Collection of people having no right to enter university (2,2)

indicatorNotes.having no: a group having no right is a GROUP that lacks its R

blocks.note: a group is a collection of people

annotation.surface: A crowd of people barred from getting into a university.
annotation.walkthrough: In British usage you 'go up' to a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge, when you start there.
annotation.definitionFit: To go up is British idiom for starting at, or returning to, university.

entries.clue: In part, Republican denies freaking out leader (9)

indicatorNotes.In: 'In part' puts the following pieces in the word PT
indicatorNotes.freaking out: someone freaking out loses composure, so DENIES loses its order

blocks.note: pt is the abbreviation for part

annotation.surface: A Republican partly denies that the leader is losing it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In part' reads as 'partly', but it splits: 'part' is PT and 'In' puts the rest inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a president heads a republic, a company or a club, one of many kinds of leader.

entries.clue: Huge fuss around finale of spectacular TV show (3,7)

indicatorNotes.around: the fuss sits around the finale, so BIG BOTHER is split to surround R

annotation.surface: A spectacular TV show ends in a huge fuss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spectacular' looks like praise for the show; only its last letter is used.
annotation.definitionFit: Big Brother is a reality TV show in which contestants live together under constant filming.

entries.clue: Holidaymaker perhaps heading for basically every Indian state, we’re told (9)

indicatorNotes.we’re told: GOA is to be heard, spelt GOER

blocks.note: Goa, the Indian state, said in a British accent, sounds like goer

annotation.surface: A tourist sets off for pretty much every state in India.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a non-rhotic (British) accent, in which GOER and GOA sound the same. Goa is famous for its beaches, so the holidaymaker fits the scene.
annotation.definitionFit: A beachgoer is someone who visits the beach, often on holiday.

entries.clue: Singing centrally features in one great new style of music (9)

indicatorNotes.features in: G is included among the fodder
indicatorNotes.new: the letters are rearranged into a new form

blocks.note: middle letter of the seven-letter singing

annotation.surface: A song's middle section appears in a great new musical genre.
annotation.walkthrough: Reggaeton is a Latin dance music that began in Puerto Rico, mixing reggae with hip-hop.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: reggaeton is one particular genre, Puerto Rican dance music with a dembow beat.

entries.clue: Pips possibly from fresh limes in a G&T (4,6)

indicatorNotes.fresh: the letters are made fresh, rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters; G&T supplies G and T

annotation.surface: Pips floating out of lime slices in a gin and tonic.
annotation.walkthrough: The pips are not fruit seeds: 'the pips' are the BBC radio beeps marking the hour, a time signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The pips broadcast on BBC radio on the hour are a time signal.

entries.clue: This month, material of mine is available to buy (2,5)

blocks.note: inst. (instant) means 'of this month' in old business letters
ore is the material dug from a mine

annotation.surface: An author announces their new material is on sale this month.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mine' looks like the possessive, but it is the pit that ore comes out of.
annotation.definitionFit: Retail idiom: a product 'in store' is stocked on the shop floor, as opposed to online only or coming soon.

entries.clue: Horned mammal seen to the south of one cold country (7)

indicatorNotes.seen to the south of: in a down clue, ELAND is written below I and C

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
the eland is an African antelope

annotation.surface: An antelope is spotted south of a chilly land.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is written backwards to the answer: the mammal comes first in the clue but last in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, and the surface's 'cold' is a nudge: the island nation sits just below the Arctic Circle.

entries.clue: Machine part broken by large blockage (4)

indicatorNotes.broken by: a thing broken by something has it forced through the middle, so L splits COG

blocks.note: a cog is a toothed machine wheel
L = large, as on clothing sizes

annotation.surface: A machine component breaks because something big has jammed it.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a jammed machine, and a clog is exactly what jams it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a clog in the drain; the verb 'to clog' is to block up.

entries.clue: The French tennis great ultimately squanders lead more than once (7)

annotation.surface: A French tennis star throws away a lead repeatedly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a sporting advantage, but it is a dog's lead. 'More than once' makes it plural.
annotation.definitionFit: Leashes are dog leads; the plural is signalled by 'more than once'.
annotation.definitionNote: 'lead more than once' stands for the plural, leads

entries.clue: Dish that’s initially covered in a tiny amount of salt (6)

annotation.surface: A recipe dish that is barely seasoned, with only a pinch of salt on it.
annotation.walkthrough: A gratin is itself a dish covered in a crust, so 'covered' suits the kitchen picture while doing the container's work.
annotation.definitionFit: A gratin is a dish topped with a browned crust of breadcrumbs or cheese.

entries.clue: When power and fury combine, shoot for the stars! (6)

indicatorNotes.combine: P and IRE are joined after AS

blocks.note: as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: A motivational slogan: harness your strength and anger and reach high.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When' is easy to read as a mere connective; it supplies AS.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom standing in for the verb: shooting for the stars is aiming very high, which is what aspiring means.

entries.clue: Certain animals, primarily horses included in my analysis info (8)

indicatorNotes.included in: something included in a group is taken inside it, so H goes inside COR

blocks.note: cor! = my!, a British exclamation of surprise
data is the information you analyse

annotation.surface: A researcher's notes on some animals, mostly horses, used in their study.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive, but it is the exclamation 'My!', which is COR in British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Chordata is the phylum of animals with a notochord, including all vertebrates.

entries.clue: I’ve nothing more to say about a fancy donut! (4,3,3)

indicatorNotes.fancy: DONUT is made into something fancy, rearranged

blocks.note: over = about, as in 'arguing over money'

annotation.surface: Someone is struck dumb by an elaborate doughnut.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over and out' is radio talk for ending a transmission, hence 'nothing more to say'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Over and out' is the radio sign-off meaning the speaker has finished.

entries.clue: Angry and tired, though not at first (3)

annotation.surface: Someone cross and weary, though they weren't to begin with.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' for tired is informal: 'my nerves are shot'.
annotation.definitionFit: Hot under the collar means angry.

entries.clue: Finest head journalist outsmarted (6)

annotation.surface: The top editor of a paper has been outwitted.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head journalist' could suggest a first letter; it is the editor, ED.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to best a rival is to get the better of them, often by wit.

entries.clue: Young relative also thus taken in by good prank periodically (8)

indicatorNotes.taken in by: AND SO sits inside G + RN

annotation.surface: A youngster is also fooled by a harmless practical joke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' means taking every other letter; here the even ones of prank.
annotation.definitionFit: A grandson is a young male relative, a child's child.
